To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the overexpression of a rice AKR gene in transgenic tobacco increases oxidative and heat tolerance by MDA and MG detoxification.

(i) OsAKR1 is induced by various abiotic stresses; (ii) the enzyme reduces reactive aldehydes including MG, a major cytotoxin of glycolysis; (iii) the enzyme is involved in MDA detoxification, a major product of lipid peroxidation; (iv) the enzyme improves oxidative and heat stress resistance in transgenic plants.
overproduction of a rice AKR in transgenic tobacco increases oxidative and heat tolerance by malondalehyde and methylglyoxl detoxification.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of a rice alko keto reductase, OsAKR1, which has been found to be involved in the detoxification of reactive carbonyls.
the role of aldo-keto reductase (AKR) enzymes in the detoxification of toxic carbonyl compounds generated in plants during oxidative and heat stress.
the role of a rice aldehyde reductase, OsAKR1, in the protection of plant cells against the toxic effects of aldehydes produced by oxidative stress.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
overexpression of OsAKR 1 gene in tobacco plants increases oxidative and heat tolerance by malondaldehyde and methylglycoxal detoxification.
the overexpression of OsAKR in transgenic tobacco leads to increased tolerance to oxidative stress generated by MV and high temperature, and to increased resistance to heat stress.
the OsAKR gene encodes a protein which is involved in the detoxification of reactive carbonyl compounds and which is upregulated by various stresses.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have shown the role of AKR1 enzyme in the detoxification of MG and MDA and the importance of these enzymes in plant tolerance against heat and oxidative stress.

we have identified a novel stress inducible rice gene encoding an aldo keto reductor (AKR) enzyme that can detoxify reactive carbonyl compounds such as MG and MDA and that overexpression of this gene results in increased tolerance to oxidative and heat stress.
the overexpression of a rice aldehyde detoxifying enzyme in transgenic tobaccots increases oxidative and heat tolerance.
The main takeaway from our work is that
AKRs are involved in plant stress response and their activity is essential for the detoxification of reactive carbonyls generated by the interaction of reactive oxygen species with membrane lipids.
the overproduction of a single aldo keto reductorase in plants can significantly increase tolerance to oxidative and heat stress by reducing malondialdehyde levels and methylglyoxyl detoxification.
OsAKR1 is a promising target to increase stress tolerance in plants and that its overproduction in plants can be achieved through transgenic approaches.
